rows.abstract: "Philippine Oceans Act of 2000".  This bill seeks to institute a maritime and oceans policy that includes a 5-year ocean development agenda. rows.abstract: Regular membership in the Philippine National Red Cross shall be open to all the adult population in the Philippines. Rationale: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has always been the recepient of mounting complaints for various abuses committed by taxi drivers for contracting with passengers instead of using their taximeters, choosing or refusing to convey passengers especially upon learning of their short destinations, arrogance, discourtesy, installing fast meters, and other similar acts. rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING ALL LOCAL CIVIL REGISTRARS WITHIN THE COUNTRY TO CAUSE AMENDMENT OF CERTAIN PORTION IN THEIR RESPECTIVE PRESCRIBED FORMS OF MARRIAGE LICENSE APPLICATIONS BY PROVIDING FOR THE INSERTION OF PRECAUTIONARY LANGUAGE FOR THE PERUSAL AND GUIDANCE OF APPLICANTS THEREOF
rows.abstract: The application for a marriage license shall contain the following statement: "THE LAWS OF THE PHILIPPINES AFFIRM YOUR RIGHT TO ENTER INTO THIS MARRIAGE AND AT THE SAME TIME TO LIVE WITHIN THE MARRIAGE FREE FROM VIOLENCE AND ABUSE. NEITHER OF YOU ISTHE PROPERTY OF THE OTHER. PHYSICAL ABUSE, SEXUAL ABUSE, AND ASSAULT OR ANY FORM OF VIOLENCE OF A SPOUSE OR OTHER FAMILY MEMBER, AS WELL AS OTHER PROVISIONS OF THE CRIMINAL LAWS OF THE PHILIPPINES, ARE APPLICABLE TO SPOUSES AND OTHER FAMILY MEMBERSAND VIOLATIONS THEREOF ARE PUNISHABLE BY LAW."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2000-03-14

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to impose upon the offender the penalties of prision correccional and prision mayor which have the same numbner of years of imprisonment for serious and less serious election offenses, respectively, under the Election Code of 1978.It likewise, seeks to INCREASE the fine of offenders to not less than one hundred thousand nor more than one million pesos, in addition to the penalty of DISQUALIFICATIO N to hold public office and deprivate of right of sufrage.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PUBLICATION IN THREE (3) NEWSPAPERS OF NATIONAL AND GENERAL CIRCULATION THE LIST OF RECOMMENDEES FOR EXECUTIVE CLEMENCY, PENALIZING THE FAILURE THEREOF, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Board of Pardons and Parole shall publish in at least three (3) newspapers of national and general circulation the names of convicts recommended for executive clemency, with their corresponding offenses and the places where committed. The publication of the names of the recommendees for executive clemency shall be made at least thirty (30) days prior to the submittal by the Chairman of the Board of Pardons and Parole to the President of the Philippines of the list of recommendees for executive clemency.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND ARTICLE 202, CHAPTER TWO, TITLE SIX OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE(VAGRANCY)
rows.abstract: RationaleL: This bill seeks to AMEND the vagrancy provision of the Revised Penal Code. Under this law, a person found loitering in any places without justifiable purpose or wandering around the streets without visible means of support is said to bea vagrant. This law is unconstitutiona l and anti-poor.  It is very susceptible to human rights abuses like any bad cop could make money out of this law or use it as a ploy to harass suspected prostitutes. It also violates the fundamental freedom ofmovement of citizens.
